Project: Kubernetes. Upgrade being assessed: 1.23 -> 1.29.
This change was introduced in release 1.25. Source: Kubernetes v1.25.0 CHANGELOG (official_changelog). Section: v1.25.0 / Changes by Kind / Deprecation.
Version facts from package metadata for this release (authoritative for version numbers): none

ITEM:
<<<
Kubeadm: during "upgrade apply/diff/node", in case the ClusterConfiguration.imageRepository stored in the "kubeadm-config" ConfigMap contains the legacy "k8s.gcr.io" repository, modify it to the new default "registry.k8s.io". Reflect the change in the in-cluster ConfigMap only during "upgrade apply".
>>>

PARENT CONTEXT (same section, for disambiguation only):
<<<
v1.25.0 / Changes by Kind / Deprecation: API server's deprecated --service-account-api-audiences flag was removed. Use --api-audiences instead. Ginkgo.Measure has been deprecated in Ginkgo V2, switch to use gomega/gmeasure instead Kube-controller-manager: Removed flags deleting-pods-qps, deleting-pods-burst, and register-retry-count. Kubeadm: during "upgrade apply/diff/node", in case the ClusterConfiguration.imageRepository stored in the "kubeadm-config" ConfigMap contains the legacy "k8s.gcr.io" repository, modify it to the new default "registry.k8s.io". Reflect the change in the in-cluster ConfigMap only during "upgrade apply". Kubeadm: graduated the kubeadm specific feature gate UnversionedKubeletConfigMap to GA and locked it to true by default. The kubelet related ConfigMap and RBAC rules are now locked to have a simplified naming *kubelet-config instead of the legacy naming *kubelet-config-x.yy, where x.yy was the version of the control plane. If you have previously used the old naming format with UnversionedKubeletConfigMap=false, you must manually copy the config map from kube-system/kubelet-config-x.yy to kube-system/kubelet-config before upgrading to v1.25. Kubeadm: stop applying the node-role.kubernetes.io/master:NoSchedule taint to control plane nodes for new clusters. Remove the taint from existing control plane nodes during "kubeadm upgrade apply" Support for the alpha seccomp annotations seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/pod and container.seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io, deprecated since v1.19, was partially removed. Kubelets no longer support the annotations, use of the annotations in static pods is no longer supported, and the seccomp annotations are no longer auto-populated when pods with seccomp fields are created. Auto-population of the seccomp fields from the annotations is planned to be removed in 1.27. Pods should use the corresponding pod or container securityContext.seccompProfile field instead. The gcp and azure auth plugins have been removed from client-go and kubectl. See https://github.com/Azure/kubelogin and https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/containers-kubernetes/kubectl-auth-changes-in-gke The beta PodSecurityPolicy admission plugin, deprecated since 1.21, is removed. Follow the instructions at https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/migrate-from-psp/ to migrate to the built-in PodSecurity admission plugin (or to another third-party policy webhook) prior to upgrading to v1.25. Decide the disposition:
- "risk": the item describes something that can break an app/deployment, require migration work, or create operational risk.
- "context": it is accurate but needs no action at 1.29 (no user action required, deprecated-but-working, additive feature). Give the reason.

For "risk", produce one or more risk paths. Use separate paths for separate symbols/APIs when they can be checked independently. Hard rules:
1. Every condition has at least one quote copied EXACTLY, character for character, from ITEM or PARENT CONTEXT (contiguous span, 3-40 words, no ellipses, no added words). Do not fix typos or formatting.
2. Each path has exactly one condition with category "version" stating that the upgrade crosses release 1.25 (quote the text that ties the change to this release, or the change statement itself), and at least one application/deployment condition (category api_usage, configuration, dependency, runtime, deployment, database, behavior or test_coverage) describing what the app or deployment must use/have for the risk to apply.
3. If the text does not state something you need, do not assert it: use role "uncertain" and explain in ambiguities. derived_by: "extraction" when the text states the fact; for an application/deployment condition ("the application uses X"), use "extraction" when the text names X as the thing affected by the change. Use "inference" only when you infer an affected symbol, scope or impact that the text does not name. Only add ambiguities for real gaps or conflicts in the text, not for the general fact that a specific application has not been inspected.
4. role: "required" (must hold), "alternative" (any one of the alternatives suffices), "optional" (raises impact), "disqualifying" (if it holds, the risk does NOT apply, e.g. not using the new opt-in API), "uncertain".
5. operator/expected_value must be checkable: e.g. operator "present" with expected_value the literal symbol; "less_than" with a version; "equals" with a setting value. expected_value is a string.
6. If a replacement API/setting/version is named, put the migration step in suggested_actions and add a condition for any behavior that differs in the replacement when the text states one.
7. search_queries: for app-side conditions with a literal symbol, give ripgrep regexes (tool "ripgrep"), kubectl commands (tool "kubectl") or SQL (tool "sql") that would find usage. Empty list if no literal symbol.
8. primary_symbol: the most specific identifier of the change (full apiVersion string like "policy/v1beta1", setting name, function, flag, or runtime name like "Python"/"Node.js"). symbols: all identifiers involved.
9. risk_level rubric: critical = upgrade fails or data is at risk for most users meeting the conditions (e.g. unsupported runtime/database version, removed API version that stops serving); high = code or config meeting the conditions breaks at upgrade; medium = behavior change or migration with a clear workaround; low = edge case, cosmetic, or warning-only.
10. fires_at: "upgrade" (at upgrade time), "first_use" (when a feature is first exercised), "rotation" (on credential/password rotation), "rollout" (on deployment rollout), "future_removal" (deprecated now, removed later).
11. applies_to: fill upgrade_method (e.g. "pg_upgrade", "dump/restore"), cluster_type, or from_versions (a version specifier like "<3.1") ONLY if the text restricts applicability; otherwise null.
Do not output confidence.

paths.path_name: kubeadm imageRepository k8s.gcr.io rewrite during upgrade
paths.description: During kubeadm upgrade apply, diff, or node, a ClusterConfiguration.imageRepository stored in the kubeadm-config ConfigMap that contains the legacy k8s.gcr.io repository is modified to the new default registry.k8s.io. The change is reflected in the in-cluster ConfigMap only during upgrade apply.

conditions.statement: The upgrade from 1.23 to 1.29 crosses release 1.25, which introduced the kubeadm imageRepository change.
quotes: Kubeadm: during "upgrade apply/diff/node", in case the ClusterConfiguration.imageRepository stored in the "kubeadm-config" ConfigMap contains the legacy "k8s.gcr.io" repository
conditions.relevance: Establishes that the change introduced in 1.25 applies to the 1.23 to 1.29 upgrade path.

conditions.statement: The cluster's kubeadm-config ConfigMap contains ClusterConfiguration.imageRepository set to the legacy k8s.gcr.io repository.
conditions.relevance: The rewrite only applies when the stored imageRepository uses the legacy k8s.gcr.io repository.
ambiguities: The text does not state what happens when imageRepository is already set to registry.k8s.io or is unset.

search_queries.query: kubectl -n kube-system get configmap kubeadm-config -o yaml

suggested_actions: Check the imageRepository value in the kube-system kubeadm-config ConfigMap before upgrading.
Confirm that registry.k8s.io is reachable from control plane and worker nodes so the rewritten repository can be used.
Review any image mirrors or pull configuration that reference k8s.gcr.io, since the stored default is changed to registry.k8s.io.
